drivingQuestion: On what principle do Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon disagree about the slaughter blood rendering the hanging limb and flesh susceptible to impurity?
outcomeNote: The unit as packaged contains only the lemma and the question; the answer falls outside this packet.

segments.en: §The mishna teaches: If «the animal was slaughtered,» Rabbi Meir holds that with the blood of the slaughtered animal the limb and the flesh were rendered susceptible to impurity. Rabbi Shimon says that they were not rendered susceptible with the animal’s own blood. The Gemara asks: «With regard to what» principle «do» Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon «disagree?»
